message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Coverage

permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  workflow_call:
    secrets:
      CODACY_PROJECT_TOKEN:
        required: true
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  coverage:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('requirements.txt', 'test-requirements.txt') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt
          pip install -r test-requirements.txt
      - name: Gather coverage data
        run: |
          python -m coverage run --source=semanticscholar/ -m unittest discover
      - name: XML reporting
        run: |
          python -m coverage xml
      - name: Codacy Coverage Reporter
        uses: codacy/codacy-coverage-reporter-action@v1
        with:
          project-token: ${{ secrets.CODACY_PROJECT_TOKEN }}
          coverage-reports: coverage.xml
",
  "rationale": "The workflow installs Python dependencies on every run without caching. Adding a pip cache keyed on requirements.txt and test-requirements.txt will reuse downloaded packages across runs, reducing installation time. This is supported by the experiment example (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) which added a similar cache step and the pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE which reports modest aggregate benefits for dependency caching.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
